youtube_title: Belle Gunness in one minute: LaPorte, Indiana's unsolved mystery (real 1908 photos)
youtube:
Belle Gunness was a widow with a farm on McClung Road in LaPorte, Indiana. Many men who answered her marriage ads were never seen again. 🕯️ On April 28, 1908, the farmhouse burned; the three children in her care died, and a woman was found in the ruins. Then searchers dug in the yard: at least a dozen people were buried there, two of them identified as men who had answered her ads, most never named. Her hired man, Ray Lamphere, was convicted of setting the fire, but no one was ever convicted of the murders. For years people said they'd seen her, and a 2008 DNA test couldn't settle it. Did Belle get away? Tell us in the comments! The full documentary, "Belle Gunness: The Black Widow of LaPorte, Indiana," is on this channel. The La Porte County Historical Society Museum's program "Belle Gunness: The Mystery Continues" is Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026 (tickets required): https://laportecountyhistory.org/ #BelleGunness #LaPorte #Indiana #TrueCrime #History #Halloween #Shorts

Photos: Belle Gunness with her children, c. 1904, George Grantham Bain Collection, Library of Congress (no known restrictions); the Gunness farm, the farm after the fire, the 1908 bird's-eye postcard and Ray Lamphere, all by Steve Shook via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 (creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0). Other pictures are drawn. Narration is a computer voice. Sources: La Porte County Historical Society; Indiana Public Media, Moment of Indiana History; Ted Hartzell, HistoryNet; Mental Floss; AP and the University of Indianapolis on the 2007-08 exhumation and DNA test; Encyclopaedia Britannica. The ad's wording is the version attributed to her in later accounts.
